name: Laryngotracheoesophageal Cleft Type 2

criteria.description: Endoscopic visualization of a cleft extending through the interarytenoid region into the posterior tracheal wall without esophageal involvement beyond the upper esophageal sphincter
Presence of feeding difficulties with aspiration and respiratory distress in the neonatal period
Radiologic evidence (esophagram or CT scan) showing abnormal communication between the larynx and trachea without extension into the esophagus
Exclusion of tracheoesophageal fistula or other congenital airway anomalies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Endoscopic visualization of the cleft combined with clinical presentation of aspiration and respiratory distress
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical and endoscopic; imaging supports but is not definitive alone.

searchTerms: endoscopic view of vocal cord cleft

common.symptomName: Failure to thrive due to feeding intolerance
searchTerms: failure to gain weight due to feeding issues

rare.symptomName: Pulmonary hypertension secondary to chronic aspiration
searchTerms: high blood pressure in lungs from aspiration
lung hypertension due to inhaled food

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests unless secondary infection present
Possible elevated inflammatory markers during aspiration pneumonia
imaging: Esophagram showing abnormal communication between larynx and trachea
CT scan of neck and chest demonstrating cleft extent
Chest X-ray showing recurrent infiltrates consistent with aspiration
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; may be sporadic or associated with syndromes like Opitz G/BBB
other: Endoscopic examination is gold standard for diagnosis
Bronchoscopy to assess cleft extent and airway involvement

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of fistulous tract between trachea and esophagus
Membranous web across the laryngeal inlet without tracheal involvement
Different clinical presentation with voice changes

redFlags: Severe aspiration pneumonia refractory to treatment
Failure to thrive despite nutritional support
references: Smith MM, et al. Laryngotracheoesophageal clefts: diagnosis and management. Int J Pediatr Otorhinolaryngol. 2020.
Holinger LD. Congenital laryngotracheoesophageal clefts. Ann Otol Rhinol Laryngol. 1989.
